paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Appearance to Solomon and the Condition for the Kingdom

answers: After Solomon had finished the building projects
Before the house of the Lord was built
During a battle
easy.explanation: The Lord appeared to Solomon after he had finished building the house of the Lord, the king’s house, and all that he desired to do.
easy.q: When did the Lord appear to Solomon?

answers: The people’s song
Solomon’s prayer and supplication
Hiram’s message
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I have heard thy prayer and thy supplication.”
easy.q: What did the Lord say He had heard?

answers: Great riches
New cities
To establish his kingdom’s throne over Israel
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to establish the throne of Solomon’s kingdom upon Israel forever.
easy.q: What did the Lord promise if Solomon walked in the ways of David?

answers: Solomon and his children had to keep the Lord’s commandments and judgments
Solomon had to conquer many lands
Hiram had to continue helping him
medium.explanation: The promise depended on walking before the Lord and keeping His statutes and judgments.
medium.q: What condition was attached to the promise concerning Solomon’s kingdom?

answers: An example or subject of common talk
A place of residence
A weapon of war
medium.explanation: In this context, Israel would become an example spoken about among the nations.
medium.q: What does the word “proverb” mean in the phrase “Israel shall be a proverb and a byword”?

answers: A lack of gold
Forsaking the Lord, serving other gods, and disobeying His commandments
Building the king’s house
medium.explanation: The Lord warned that turning from Him and worshipping other gods would bring judgment.
medium.q: What could cause Israel to lose the land and the house?

answers: The holiness of the house would not protect Israel if they forsook the Lord
The house would remain secure even if Israel worshipped other gods
The house depended only on the amount of gold in it
challenge.explanation: Although the Lord had hallowed the house, He warned that Israel’s disobedience would bring judgment upon both the people and the house.
challenge.q: What relationship do these verses show between the house and Israel’s conduct?

answers: Building versus commerce
The promise of kingdom and blessing versus the warning of exile and ruin
Jerusalem versus Egypt
challenge.explanation: The Lord promised an enduring kingdom for obedience but warned of removal from the land and disgrace among the nations for disobedience.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the Lord’s words to Solomon?

answers: David was an example of walking in integrity and uprightness
David had built the king’s house
David had helped Hiram
challenge.explanation: David was presented as one who walked before the Lord in integrity of heart and uprightness.
challenge.q: Why did the Lord mention David in His message to Solomon?

short_answers.question: What had Solomon finished when the Lord appeared to him?
short_answers.answer: He had finished building the house of the Lord, the king’s house, and all that he desired to do.

short_answers.question: What would happen if Israel turned from the Lord and worshipped other gods?
short_answers.answer: The Lord would cut Israel off from the land and cast the house out of His sight.

short_answers.question: Why would people passing by the house be astonished and hiss?
short_answers.answer: They would wonder why the Lord had brought such evil upon the land and the house.
short_answers.explanation: The question and its answer are given in verses 8–9.

paragraphs.title: The Towns Given to Hiram and the Gold from Tyre

answers: Ten cities
Twenty cities
Fifty cities
easy.explanation: Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
easy.q: How many cities did Solomon give to Hiram?

answers: Cedar trees, fir trees, and gold
Iron and horses
Water and grain
easy.explanation: Hiram had furnished Solomon with cedar trees, fir trees, and gold.
easy.q: What materials had Hiram supplied to Solomon?

answers: He was very pleased
He built a temple in them
They did not please him
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “they pleased him not.”
easy.q: How did Hiram feel about the cities he received?

answers: The cities were given after Hiram supplied building materials and gold
Hiram received the cities before he knew Solomon
The cities were given in exchange only for ships
medium.explanation: After describing Hiram’s supplies, the passage says that Solomon gave him twenty cities.
medium.q: What was the connection between Hiram’s assistance and the cities Solomon gave him?

answers: According to everything he wanted or needed
According to all the cities in the kingdom
According to all the soldiers
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Hiram supplied Solomon with everything he desired in that context.
medium.q: What does “according to all his desire” mean in this passage?

answers: To see the cities Solomon had given him
To bring gold from Ophir
To build the house of the Lord
medium.explanation: Hiram came from Tyre to see the cities given to him by Solomon.
medium.q: Why did Hiram come out from Tyre?

answers: He did not consider them a satisfactory or suitable gift
He did not know that they belonged to Solomon
He wanted to exchange them for gold from Ophir
challenge.explanation: The cities did not please Hiram, and he called the region the land of Cabul.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Hiram’s response to the cities?

answers: Twenty cities and sixscore talents of gold
Three cities and ten talents of silver
One hundred ships and four hundred horses
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions twenty cities and sixscore, or one hundred twenty, talents of gold.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the wealth exchanged between Solomon and Hiram?

answers: Hiram sent gold, Solomon gave cities, and then Hiram saw them
Solomon gave cities, Hiram saw them, and then Hiram sent gold
Hiram saw the cities, Solomon built Tyre, and then the cities were given
challenge.explanation: The cities were given first, Hiram inspected them next, and he sent gold afterward.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

short_answers.question: Where were the cities that Solomon gave Hiram located?
short_answers.answer: They were in the land of Galilee.

short_answers.question: What name did Hiram give the region?
short_answers.answer: He called it the land of Cabul.
short_answers.explanation: Hiram used this name after seeing the cities.

short_answers.question: How much gold did Hiram send to Solomon?
short_answers.answer: He sent sixscore talents of gold.

paragraphs.title: Building Projects, Forced Labor, and Fortified Cities

answers: To build the house of the Lord, his own house, and the cities
To send ships to Ophir
To buy cedar trees from Hiram
easy.explanation: The levy supported Solomon’s building projects, including the Temple, the palace, Millo, Jerusalem’s wall, and several cities.
easy.q: Why did Solomon raise a levy of bondservice?

answers: Hazor
Gezer
Baalath
easy.explanation: Pharaoh took Gezer, burned it, and gave it as a present to his daughter.
easy.q: Which city did Pharaoh capture and give to his daughter, Solomon’s wife?

answers: The peoples remaining in the land who were not children of Israel
Only the children of Israel
Only the officers of the chariots
easy.explanation: The remaining Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites were placed under this service.
easy.q: Who was placed under tribute of bondservice?

answers: Compulsory labor imposed upon people
A tax paid only in gold
A voluntary gift to the king
medium.explanation: Bondservice was required labor for the king’s building projects.
medium.q: What does “bondservice” mean in this passage?

answers: The remaining peoples were placed under bondservice, while the Israelites were not made bondmen
The Israelites worked while foreigners served in the army
Everyone performed the same work
medium.explanation: The passage says Solomon made no bondmen of the children of Israel, but levied bondservice upon the other peoples.
medium.q: What distinction was made between the Israelites and the peoples remaining in the land?

answers: Pharaoh built Gezer and Solomon burned it
Pharaoh took and burned Gezer, then gave it to his daughter
Solomon gave Gezer to Pharaoh for gold
medium.explanation: Pharaoh captured Gezer, burned it, slew the Canaanites, and gave the city to his daughter.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes Pharaoh’s connection with Gezer?

answers: The passage mentions cities for chariots and cities for horsemen
The passage mentions only the house of the Lord
The passage mentions only Pharaoh’s gift
challenge.explanation: Cities for chariots and horsemen show the military organization of Solomon’s kingdom.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Solomon built military centers as well as royal buildings?

answers: The passage presents a division of roles and status within Solomon’s kingdom
All the inhabitants were slaves
The passage describes only the work of priests
challenge.explanation: The text distinguishes Israelites as men of war, servants, princes, captains, and rulers, while the remaining peoples performed bondservice.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the different roles assigned to Israelites and foreigners?

answers: The mention of Hazor, Megiddo, Gezer, Bethhoron, Baalath, Tadmor, and other cities
The mention of Solomon’s prayer alone
The mention of Hiram’s gold alone
challenge.explanation: The list of cities shows that Solomon’s construction reached throughout his dominion.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the building projects extended beyond Jerusalem?

short_answers.question: What was the levy used to build?
short_answers.answer: It was used to build the house of the Lord, Solomon’s house, Millo, Jerusalem’s wall, and several cities.
short_answers.explanation: These projects are listed in verses 15–19.

short_answers.question: What did Solomon make of the children of Israel?
short_answers.answer: He made them men of war, servants, princes, captains, and rulers of his chariots and horsemen.
short_answers.explanation: Their roles are described in verse 22.

short_answers.question: How many chief officers were over Solomon’s work?
short_answers.answer: There were five hundred and fifty chief officers.
short_answers.explanation: This number is given in verse 23.

paragraphs.title: Temple Worship and the Fleet to Ophir

answers: Once
Three times
Twenty times
easy.explanation: Solomon offered them three times in a year.
easy.q: How many times a year did Solomon offer burnt offerings and peace offerings?

answers: Ezion-geber
Gezer
Tyre
easy.explanation: He made the navy in Ezion-geber, beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea.
easy.q: Where did Solomon make his navy of ships?

answers: Cedar trees
Gold
Horses
easy.explanation: They fetched four hundred and twenty talents of gold from Ophir.
easy.q: What did Solomon and his servants bring back from Ophir?

answers: The officers of Jerusalem
Hiram’s servants, shipmen who had knowledge of the sea
Pharaoh’s sons
medium.explanation: Hiram sent servants who were shipmen with knowledge of the sea, together with Solomon’s servants.
medium.q: Who helped Solomon operate the navy?

answers: Men experienced in sailing and seafaring
Men who lived near the wilderness
Men who worked in the house of the Lord
medium.q: What does “shipmen that had knowledge of the sea” mean?

answers: After the description of Temple worship, the passage describes a fleet that brought gold
The fleet was built before the altar was made
The offerings were used to pay Hiram
medium.explanation: The passage first describes Solomon’s offerings and completion of the house, then his fleet and its voyage to Ophir.
medium.q: How are the two parts of this passage connected?

answers: It included both religious activity and maritime commerce
It was devoted only to trade
It abandoned Temple worship
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both regular worship and a seafaring expedition for gold.
challenge.q: What does the combination of Temple worship and the fleet reveal about Solomon’s kingdom?

answers: It amounted to four hundred and twenty talents
It was sent from Gezer
It was brought by Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically states that the fleet fetched four hundred and twenty talents of gold.
challenge.q: Which detail about the gold from Ophir is easy to overlook?

answers: They were shipmen with knowledge of the sea
They were builders of the king’s house
They were officers over the forced labor
challenge.explanation: Hiram’s servants were experienced sailors who helped operate the navy.
challenge.q: What special role did Hiram’s men have on the voyage to Ophir?

short_answers.question: What did Solomon offer on the altar three times a year?
short_answers.answer: He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings and burned incense before the Lord.

short_answers.question: Where was Ezion-geber located?
short_answers.answer: It was beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom.
short_answers.explanation: The location is given in verse 26.

short_answers.question: How much gold was brought from Ophir?
short_answers.answer: Four hundred and twenty talents of gold.
short_answers.explanation: The amount is stated in verse 28.
